newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Anglo American has entered a new phase in its evolution into a focused industrial and mining financial group by launching a strategic review which is likely to lead to the group disposing of non-core assets.
- Police were investigating fraud cases involving 300 million rand in the KwaZulu-Natal government, auditor-general Chris Foster said on Monday.
- Hopes of an inclusive constitutional settlement were dashed on Monday when the IFP told the ANC it was not returning to the Constitutional Assembly.
- French banking group Societe Generale was set to buy local broking firm Frankel Pollak during the next week, market sources said on Monday.
- A smear campaign by a local business man to deter foreign investors from putting their money into South Africa has been brought to the attention of Thabo Mbeki, the deputy president.

- Mossgas, the much-maligned fuel-from-gas producer, is negotiating several joint ventures, including offshore gas exploration and an onshore chemical plant, David Day, its chief executive, said on Monday.

- The European Union has revised its stainless steel specifications, a move which could put a squeeze on South African exports and boost the competitiveness of imports unless local industry adapts to these new standards, David Slater, the executive director of the Southern African Stainless Steel Development Association, said on Monday.
- Suspected Irish Republican guerillas bombed Britain's army headquarters in Northern Ireland on Monday, injuring 31 people, and shattering an uneasy two-year peace in the province.

- The 2,000 South African Airways engineering and technical staff who have been on a work-to-rule since Wednesday have been given until noon on Tuesday to resume normal duties or face being locked out from SAA premises without pay.
- Relatives and friends of the dozens of women who were allegedly raped and murdered by serial killer accused Moses Sithole have demanded that the death sentence be reinstated.
- South Africa moved a step closer to the finalisation of the draft constitution when parties on Monday reached an agreement on all eight clauses which were rejected by the Constitutional Court.
